messages:
maya: Quick note — observed sustained saturation on primary model `redwood-v1` in us-west for several startup tenants. Some requests are timing out at LB while autoscale spins up. We currently fallback to quantized variants only by hard routing rules, but console shows no per-tenant fallback rate. Need policy + API + console changes to support capacity-driven implicit fallbacks.
liam: Agree, we should make implicit fallback first-class. Two asks: 1) routing policy grammar so ops can opt tenants in/out, 2) response metadata so customers can detect fallback.
kevin: For response metadata: propose `x-redwood-variant` header plus structured telemetry events to the Console. Clients can read header to log and we can show breakdown in per-route dashboard.
anita: Billing + quota question: if a startup request falls back to a smaller variant (cheaper), do we bill the original model or the actual variant? This matters for reserved capacity vs hosted usage.
sam: We should default to charging based on the variant executed (actual GPU cost). But surface an audit field so ops can do chargeback mapping. Also limit automatic fallback for tiers that paid for dedicated capacity.
maya: Design proposal (high level): automatic fallback when: primary is at 95% capacity OR queue latency > 200ms and compatible variant exists in same region. Rules: prefer same-region, respect tenant tier allowlist/denylist, try KV-cache compatible variants first to avoid cold-cache latency hit.
liam: Compatibility check note: fallback should only be allowed if tokenizer + architecture are cache-compatible. For example, gpt-like -> quantized-gpt OK; branching to different vocab/model families is not.
kevin: Console telemetry items we need: per-tenant fallback_rate (ratio), fallback_latency_delta histogram, fallback_variant_map (counts), and a time series alert when fallback_rate > 5% for 10m. Also show a togglable annotation on rollout traces when requests hit fallback.
anita: UX: In the Deployment rollouts page, add a column "Fallback exposure" showing percent of calls diverted and an action to disable auto-fallback for that deployment. For Dedicated customers, default auto-fallback = false.
sam: API surface: New routing policy block in tenant config. Example: 
```
"fallback_policy": {
  "strategy": "capacity_first",
  "prefer_same_region": true,
  "allow_by_tier": {"enterprise": false, "startup": true},
  "max_latency_ms": 500
}
```
This is server-side only.
kevin: And response header example: `X-Redwood-Variant: redwood-v1-quantized; fallback_reason=capacity; fallback_from=redwood-v1`
liam: Also emit a structured event to tracing: `event:variant_fallback`, fields: tenant_id, from_variant, to_variant, reason, latency_ms_before, latency_ms_after. Console can join this with request traces.
maya: Ops concerns: we need a backstop to avoid cascading fallbacks. If fallback variant saturates, don't keep demoting — cap to two levels and then queue or fail. Also a circuit-breaker per-tenant to stop trying fallback for N failures.
anita: Agree on circuit-breaker. And a per-tenant override API: `POST /v1/tenants/:id/fallback-config` for account teams.
liam: Small compatibility implementation detail: prefer routing to warm pools that already have KV caches for that tenant. We can check `cache_hit_rate` tag on pool. If not compatible, include in telemetry that fallback caused cold-warm penalty.
kevin: Telemetry rollout plan: start with a read-only flag `enable_fallback_reporting` for 24h to gather baseline, then enable enforcement. Ops can use metrics to tune thresholds.
sam: Deploy-bot: deploy queued by @deploy-bot:infra at 2024-07-18 19:02Z — will land initial routing policy parser and header emission.
maya: Next steps: (1) PR for routing grammar + circuit breaker (liam), (2) API proposal for tenant override + billing mapping (anita), (3) Console mockups for fallback exposure graphs (kevin), (4) rollout plan: 48h telemetry-only, then opt-in enablement per-region.
liam: I'll start the PR and add unit tests for compatibility checks.
anita: I'll draft billing guidance and default charge policy.
kevin: I'll wire up dashboard panels and the alert rule.
sam: I'll coordinate the deploys and add an ops runbook for investigating high fallback rates.
maya: Thanks — want a short sync tomorrow to sign off on defaults before telemetry-only rollouts. :thumbsup:
